claims.text: The baseline material is an as-cast HfMoTaTiZr high-entropy alloy.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
Selective laser melting can create a hierarchical porous microstructure in HfMoTaTiZr.
The proposed SLM parameters are 200 W laser power, 800 mm/s scanning speed, and 30 μm layer thickness.
The proposed SLM process will produce a 10% porosity level.
Introducing the hierarchical porous microstructure will reduce the alloy's bulk density.
An optimized pore distribution will maintain the alloy's mechanical properties.
The porous microstructure will increase surface area.
The increased surface area will enhance the alloy's strength and toughness.
The intervention can reduce density by as much as 15%, from 10.21 to approximately 8.68 g cm−3.
The SLM-processed material will retain yield strength within 5% of the as-cast material under tensile loading from room temperature through 1000 °C.
The SLM-processed material will retain ultimate tensile strength within 5% of the as-cast material under tensile loading from room temperature through 1000 °C.
The predicted density reduction and mechanical-property retention depend on the SLM parameters and resulting microstructure.

contradictions.description: The specified porosity is 10%, while the predicted bulk-density reduction is as high as 15%; no additional composition or phase change is specified to explain the extra reduction.

The predicted strength-retention criterion is within 5% of the as-cast values, but the hypothesis is rejected only for losses greater than 10%, leaving a 5–10% loss that fails the stated prediction without triggering falsification.
The hypothesis describes a density reduction 'up to 15%,' which does not establish a minimum reduction, whereas the falsification rule requires at least a 10% reduction.
